candidates: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion with Neovascularization
key_facts: Macular edema completely resolved at 3 months
OCTA findings at 6 months showed no abnormality
OCTA findings at 12 months showed hyperreflective tissues on retinal vessels
OCTA findings at 15 months showed increased hyperreflective tissues with angiogenic sprouts
OCTA findings at 18 months showed development in area of preexisting proliferation
OCTA findings at 21 months showed enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface
Fluorescein Angiography at 21 months showed dendritic vascular-like structures

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with macular edema, followed by the development of hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts on OCTA, and dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography, is consistent with the progression of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, which is characterized by the formation of new, fragile blood vessels in the retina.

rejected.label: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion with Neovascularization
rejected.why: There is no mention of a branch retinal vein occlusion in the vignette, and the development of neovascularization is not limited to the area of the occlusion.

rejected.label: Retinal Vein Occlusion with Neovascularization
rejected.why: Similar to branch retinal vein occlusion, there is no mention of a retinal vein occlusion in the vignette, and the neovascularization is not consistent with the typical presentation of a retinal vein occlusion.

rejected.label: Choroidal Neovascularization
rejected.why: The OCTA and Fluorescein Angiography findings suggest retinal neovascularization, rather than choroidal neovascularization, which would typically involve the choroid and not the retina.
